newsitem.title: USA: Cargill Inc unit to make bags from corn polymer.
newsitem.headline: Cargill Inc unit to make bags from corn polymer.

text.p: Cargill Inc said it will market a new line of biodegradable lawn and leaf bags made from corn and other farm products from early next year.
The 30-gallon plastic bags are designed expressly for collecting yard waste as part of municipal compost programs and offer an alternative to kraft-paper bags, Cargill said.
Cargill's EcoPLA Business Unit and Duro Bag Manufacturing Co of Ludlow, Ky., have agreed to market the bags from early in 1997 after test marketing in Minnesota this fall.

The EcoPLA Business Unit was established in Cargill's North American Corn Milling Division in 1989 to develop production and applications for polylactic acid, the primary component in EcoPLA Renewable Biopolymer, a biodegradable resin.
